<thought>Based on the ESI mass spectrum, the most intense peak at m/z ≈ 199 shows a strong M+2 isotope with nearly equal intensity, which is characteristic of a bromine‑containing compound (Br has a 1:1 M/M+2 isotopic pattern). Subtracting the mass of a proton (1.007 Da) gives a neutral monoisotopic mass of ≈ 197.99 Da. Accounting for one bromine atom (≈ 78.918 Da) leaves ≈ 119.07 Da to be composed of C, H, and O. The combination C₈H₇O (96 + 7.055 + 15.995 ≈ 119.05 Da) matches this remainder closely, giving a total formula C₈H₇OBr with a calculated monoisotopic mass of 197.968 Da (≈ 0.025 Da below the observed value, within typical experimental error). Therefore the most plausible molecular formula is C₈H₇OBr. </thought>
<final_answer>C8H7OBr</final_answer>
